comments.body: Hmmm, I prefer how it was before; not sure about #411 either.
The provided screenshot is nice. We need a big top right github button still to easily give access to the github repo

In the end a fixed left menu only work if you limit the left menu items to a fixed number. The more they grow the more it will be hard to fit them all in the left column (thus weird scrollbars etc).

As for #411 I think I put what seemed obvious to me in it: big buttons and contrast at important spot while most users will not need them. Yes we need to show we are on github, not at a fixed css position I feel.

> The provided screenshot is nice

I disagree, having the stackoverflow button "hidden" at the bottom of the menu doesn't make sense.

> I disagree, having the stackoverflow button "hidden" at the bottom of the menu doesn't make sense.

Yes ok.

TBH I think I do not see the exact value of linking to stackoverflow since I would first go to github issues. I would have a hard time deciding if I need to post on stackoverflow OR github since I have both links = Should we split our issues between SO and github right away, how will the user decides?
The most common reflex for developers is to go to stackoverflow, I think. Not much people go for github to get their problem fixed.

> The most common reflex for developers is to go to stackoverflow, I think. Not much people go for github to get their problem fixed.

Yes but would you use the instantsearch documentation website to then click on stackoverflow icon?
